projects.name: Property Address Classification
projects.desc: 5-class text classifier for property addresses, benchmarked across four model families
features: Classifies 11.6K property addresses into 5 categories (Flat, Plot, House, Shop, Commercial Unit)
Benchmarks Logistic Regression, Random Forest, XGBoost and LightGBM; the tuned XGBoost model reaches 90.8% accuracy and 89.5% macro F1
5,027 features: TF-IDF unigrams and bigrams plus 27 custom features such as floor, unit and plot detection
DistilBERT fine-tuned as a transformer baseline
Unit tests for preprocessing and feature engineering, plus per-class error analysis
challenges: Severe class imbalance. SMOTE was tried and rejected because it produced nonsense addresses, so the final model uses scale_pos_weight with stratified splits.
TF-IDF at 10,000 features overfit, so it was cut to 5,000 and supplemented with custom domain features.
Choosing a metric: macro F1 instead of accuracy, so the small classes are not hidden by the large ones.
DistilBERT scored about 93% but took 5 to 8 hours to train on CPU, so it stayed a baseline rather than the shipped model.

projects.name: Loan Recommendation System
projects.desc: Five ML models that recommend loan eligibility, amount, rate, product and tenure
features: Five scikit-learn models: eligibility, loan amount, interest rate, product and tenure
FastAPI backend with PostgreSQL, containerised with Docker
CIBIL score validation against a local credit database
EMI comparison between loan options
Next.js frontend on Vercel, Python API on Render
challenges: Predicting five different targets from one applicant profile, each with its own model and encoders.
Keeping the label encoders and models consistent between training and prediction so inputs are encoded identically.
Validating the applicant's CIBIL score before any recommendation is returned.
Running a Next.js frontend and a Python API as two separately deployed repositories.

projects.name: Los Angeles Traffic Prediction
projects.desc: Traffic congestion analysis and forecasting for Los Angeles
features: Forecasts congestion with Random Forest and Support Vector Regression
Uses historical traffic, weather conditions and special events as inputs
Clustering, correlation analysis and anomaly detection to find high-incident intersections
Interactive HTML traffic and heat maps
challenges: Cleaning a large traffic dataset with missing and inconsistent values before modelling.
Combining traffic history with weather and special-event data.
Interactive maps get heavy on large data, so an optimised map was produced alongside the full one.

projects.name: Warehouse Dashboard
projects.desc: Inventory, shipment and supplier dashboard with full create, edit and delete
features: Overview with live KPIs, stock by category, shipment status and a low-stock list
Inventory, shipments and suppliers pages with search, filter, sort, export, and create, edit and delete
Analytics computed in SQL with GROUP BY instead of in Python
Eager loading removes the N+1 query problem, checked by query-count tests
Day shift and night shift themes, usable on phones
challenges: Listing items with their suppliers issued one query per row. Joined eager loading fixed it, and a test counts queries to keep it fixed.
Dashboard totals were first summed in Python. Moving them to SQL aggregates keeps the work in the database.
Deleting a supplier that still has items has to be refused with a clear 409 rather than a crash.
Redesigned the interface away from the default Material look into a packing-slip style with shipping-label cards and stamped status tags.

projects.name: GeriRisk
projects.desc: Wearable-data health risk prediction for elderly care
features: Three scikit-learn models score cardiac stress, fall likelihood and respiratory irregularity
Risk shown as High, Moderate or Low in an alert-driven caregiver dashboard
CSV upload pipeline for wearable data with validation and feature aggregation
Standalone FastAPI inference service, deployed independently from the web app
challenges: Turning raw wearable readings (heart rate, SpO2, steps, sleep, temperature) into features the models can score.
Validating uploaded CSV files before they reach the models.
Keeping the Next.js app and the Python inference service as two separate deployments.

projects.name: E-Commerce Platform
projects.desc: Full stack store with catalog, cart, authentication, orders and admin dashboard
features: Product catalog with category browsing and filtering
Shopping cart, user registration and login
Order management and an admin dashboard
React frontend on Vercel, Dockerised Spring Boot API on Render, MongoDB Atlas
challenges: Configuring CORS between a Vercel frontend and a Render backend.
Moving from a local MongoDB to Atlas and seeding product data with a script.
Running the same Spring Boot service locally and in a Docker container on Render.

projects.name: Webhook Ingest Service
projects.desc: Go webhook service where I found and fixed eight reported defects
features: Receives call-completion webhooks and keeps per-account call stats
Idempotent writes: a unique index with INSERT ... ON CONFLICT DO NOTHING in one transaction
Layered structure: http api, ingest, store and stats packages
A failing test for each fix, run with the Go race detector
challenges: 50 simultaneous deliveries of one event stored 36 copies. A unique index and one transaction fixed it.
An unlocked in-memory cache lost updates under load, found with the race detector.
A background update ran on an already-cancelled request context and failed silently.
In-flight recording work was lost on shutdown because goroutines were not tracked.

projects.name: Real-Time Chat Application
projects.desc: WebSocket chat application built with Spring Boot
features: Real-time messaging over a Spring Boot WebSocket handler
Messages saved to SQLite and replayed as history
Automatic reconnection when the connection drops
Mobile-responsive interface, Docker support
challenges: Broadcasting each message to every connected client from one WebSocket handler.
Persisting messages through a Spring repository so history survives a restart.
Reconnecting cleanly in the browser after a dropped connection.
Packaging the Spring Boot app in Docker for deployment on Render.

projects.name: FlowBit
projects.desc: Multi-agent pipeline that classifies emails, JSON and PDFs and routes follow-up actions
features: A Gemini 1.5 Flash classifier decides the input format and business intent
Specialist agents for email, JSON and PDF inputs
Action router for CRM, risk alert, compliance and notification follow-ups, with 3 retries and exponential backoff
Every request recorded with status and history endpoints
challenges: LLM output is not always valid JSON, so the classifier strips code fences, extracts the first JSON object and falls back to a heuristic at 0.5 confidence.
Validating incoming JSON against fixed schemas before an agent handles it.
Retrying failed downstream actions without losing the request, with a mock fallback when a target is unavailable.
